***Added "ThisTurnEntered" mode to Count$. It lets you access how many cards of any type were put into a certain zone this turn (and from where,if that needs limiting)**

 * Examples: SVar:X:Count$ThisTurnEntered Graveyard Card &#x3D; Returns the number of cards put into a graveyard from anywhere this turn.
 * SVar:X:Count$ThisTurnEntered Exile from Battlefield Creature &#x3D; Returns the number of creatures exiled from the battlefield this turn.
 * The count is reset on end of turn.

[2e6ec8e4b8c25fe](https://github.com/gizatt/forge/commit/2e6ec8e4b8c25fe) jendave *2011-08-06 21:01:56*

***Fixed the most cornery of theoretical corner cases yet. (If the card that recieves the trigger object with ID 0 at launchtime is in a match with a card whose triggers are taken away (usually something animated), the animated cards trigger would get ID 0 because IDs are reset to 0 at every newGame() and when that is supposed to be removed TriggerHandler would remove Trigger ID 0, being the card that recieved the trigger object at launchtime, so the animated will keep it's trigger when it shouldn't and the launctime card will lose it's trigger when it shouldn't! Solution: Reset IDs to 50000 on newGame() instead. Simple. :))**

***"Optional$" parameter for triggers is now "OptionalDecider$" which works as "Defined$" for players.**

 * Old &quot;Optional$ True&quot; is equivalent to &quot;OptionalDecider$ You&quot;, old &quot;Optional$ OpponentDecides&quot; &#x3D; &quot;OptionalDecider$ Opponent&quot; of course and instead of &quot;Optional$ TriggeredControllerDecides&quot; you can use any of the Triggered-variables that return a player.
 * AF_Token&#x27;s &quot;TokenOwner$&quot; parameter is now also a &quot;Defined$&quot;-like.
 * Updated all cards that used either (637 of them!)

[94db7c2f32b356f](https://github.com/gizatt/forge/commit/94db7c2f32b356f) jendave *2011-08-06 19:25:22*

***Added mode specific trigger parameters. They are: (Explanations in parenthesis)**

 * AttackerBlocked &#x3D; Attacker,Blocker
 * AttackerUnblocked &#x3D; Attacker
 * Attacks &#x3D; Attacker
 * Blocks &#x3D; Attacker,Blocker
 * ChangesZone &#x3D; Card(The card that was moved)
 * CounterAdded &#x3D; Card(The card that got the counter(s))
 * Cycled &#x3D; Card(The card that was cycled)
 * DamageDone &#x3D; Source(The card that dealt the damage),Target(The card or player who recieved the damage),DamageAmount(The amount of damage that was dealt) [BEWARE: Since Target can be both a card or a player object, you must take care to match it with your ValidTarget parameter!]
 * Discarded &#x3D; Card(The card that was discarded)
 * Drawn &#x3D; Card(The card that was drawn)
 * LandPlayed &#x3D; Card(The card that was played)
 * LifeGained &#x3D; Player(The player who gained life),LifeAmount(The amount of life that was gained)
 * LifeLost &#x3D; Player(The player who lost life),LifeAmount(The amount of life that was lost)
 * Phase &#x3D; Player(The player whose turn it is)
 * Sacrificed &#x3D; Card(The card that was sacrificed)
 * SpellAbilityCast &#x3D; Card(The card of the spell or ability)
 * Taps &#x3D; Card(The card that was tapped)
 * TurnFaceUp &#x3D; Card(The card that was turned face up)
 * Untaps &#x3D; Card(The card that was untapped)
 * To use a parameter, simply call it like this: &quot;Triggered&lt;Parameter Name&gt;&quot;. To get the controller or owner of a card parameter, append Controller or Owner. For example: &quot;TriggeredAttackerController&quot;.
 * Parameters that don&#x27;t return an integer (i.e. the ones that have &quot;Amount&quot; in their name) can be used for Defined$ parameters or to get additional info from, a&#x27;la &quot;SVar:X:TriggeredBlocker$CardPower&quot;.
 * Parameters that DO return an integer can only be accessed via Count$ like this: &quot;Count$TriggeredLifeAmount&quot;.
 * Updated all cards that use Triggered to their new respective parameters.

[36094b93913c36f](https://github.com/gizatt/forge/commit/36094b93913c36f) jendave *2011-08-06 04:23:33*

**added Generic aura handling code.**

 * It will accept keywords of the form:
 * Enchant &lt;type&gt; [Curse]
 * Enchant - all will have this
 * &lt;type&gt; - currently [Artifact, Creature, Land, Enchantment]
 * [Curse] - if this word is present, AI will target human&#x27;s permanents.
 * This allows (for example) for Blight to be implemented as:
 * Blight
 * B B
 * Enchantment Aura
 * When enchanted land becomes tapped, destroy it.
 * Enchant Land Curse
 * And all you have to do it add the appropriate resolution code to GameActionUtil.executeTapSideEffects():
